newsitem.title: USA: Dlr treads water at US noon, sterling washed away.
newsitem.headline: Dlr treads water at US noon, sterling washed away.

text.p: The dollar was quietly mixed at noon, suffering from neglect as the market's attention was diverted to a sharp decline in the pound, dealers said.

The pound tumbled against the dollar and mark after a poll showed the British Labor Party's wide lead over the governing Conservative Party had narrowed dramatically, barely one week before the U.K. general election, dealers said.
"... There is some concern you could could end up with a hung parliament," said Tom Hoge, a vice president of corporate foreign exchange at Bank of New York.
"There is no doubt there has been some real good selling in sterling. I would say it's been the most active currency of the day by far. Everything else is pretty calm," Hoge said.
The dollar eased slightly to 1.7115/25 marks at noon, from 1.7148/53 at the open. But dollar/yen was up a tad to 126.15/25 from 126.07/17.
The pound, meanwhile, was near its session low, licking its wounds at $1.6205/15, compared to $1.6312/22 at the U.S. open and near 2.7775 marks, off from about 2.7980 in early trade.

An opinion poll in the UK's Guardian newspaper on Wednesday slashed Labor's lead to just five percentage points from 14 points, the first time a survey has shown the opposition's lead slip to single digits since late 1993.

In addition, the Tory Party said on Wednesday that its private polling showed that it was trailing Labor by less than 10 percentage points every day in the past week. The voters will cast their ballots on May 1.
The pound has been supported by speculation that the Labor party would be a shoo-in and would quickly tighten credit, ending Tory foot-dragging, dealers said.
The dollar held its ground above 1.71 marks and 126 yen during the New York session.

Dealers said the greenback was still warm from Tuesday's near-record run up in Wall Street stocks, even though U.S. financial markets cooled a bit on Wednesday. The Dow industrials were nearly flat and Treasuries were off at noon.

"The dollar is consolidating in a trading range after the big move up yesterday," said John Nelson, foreign exchange trading manager at ABN-AMRO Bank. "It seems to be benefitting from what is going on in U.S. dollar-denominated assets."

But the market remains on edge in advance of Sunday's gathering of central bankers and finance ministers from the seven big industrial nations. The G7 may try to craft a somewhat tougher statement on the dollar's rise than they delivered at February's Berlin meeting, traders said.
But they will probably tread very gingerly around the issue of intervention, for fear of a major flop in the dollar.

"There are some rumors that after the G7 they will issue a stronger statement regarding the current dollar (level). That may rattle the market a little bit," said Jeffrey Yu, senior currency dealer at Sanwa Bank Ltd.
"Probably they want to talk amongst themselves about how to engineer a slow rise of dollar without actually intervening in the market," Yu said.
Dollar/yen was capped by offers between 126.50 and 127, dealers said. Options-related stop-loss buy orders are expected above 127.10 yen.
Mark/yen firmed slightly. Sellers are expected to jump in on a break below 73.40 yen and buying should kick in over 74.05, traders said.
Elsewhere, the dollar eased to 1.4620/30 Swiss francs from 1.4641/46 and rose to Canadian $1.3940/45 from C$1.3920/25.
((--Alden Bentley, 212 859 1667))
